# clang-tidy

## What problem does clang-tidy solve?

`clang-format` enforces style — where to put braces, how to align operands, how many spaces to use. That is purely cosmetic.

**clang-tidy** goes deeper: it is a static analysis and linting tool that reads your code semantically and detects actual bugs, anti-patterns, and violations of best practices — things a compiler warning will never catch.

Examples of what clang-tidy finds:

- Dereferencing a moved-from object (`bugprone-use-after-move`)
- Forgetting `[[nodiscard]]` on a function that returns an error code (`modernize-use-nodiscard`)
- A loop variable that copies instead of binding by reference (`performance-for-range-copy`)
- Using a raw C cast where `static_cast` would be safer (`cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-cstyle-cast`)
- A signed/unsigned comparison that silently wraps (`bugprone-signed-char-misuse`)

Catching these at static-analysis time — before tests, before code review — is far cheaper than diagnosing a runtime failure or a security vulnerability.

---

## How it works

clang-tidy is a **Clang-based** tool. It parses source files with the full Clang frontend (not just a text scanner), which means it understands templates, macros, overload resolution, and all of C++23. Its diagnostics are as precise as a compiler error.

It needs a **compile commands database** (`compile_commands.json`) to know the exact flags (include paths, defines, standard version) used to build each file. CMake generates this file automatically when configured with `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON`, which this project's `configure` target already sets.

---

## Makefile targets

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `make tidy` | Run clang-tidy and report all issues (no modifications) |
| `make tidy-fix` | Run clang-tidy and apply auto-fixes where possible |
| `make tidy-check` | CI gate — same as `tidy` but exits non-zero on any issue |

All three targets require `make configure` (or `make rebuild`) to have been run first, since they depend on `production-builds/release/compile_commands.json`.

---

## Configuration file

Rules live in `.clang-tidy` at the root of the repository. clang-tidy discovers it automatically when run from anywhere in the tree.

### Check groups enabled

| Group | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `clang-analyzer-*` | Clang's built-in static analyzer: null dereferences, dead code, memory leaks, API misuse |
| `bugprone-*` | Common bug patterns: use-after-move, integer overflow, suspicious string operations |
| `cppcoreguidelines-*` | C++ Core Guidelines (Stroustrup/Herb Sutter): ownership, type safety, resource management |
| `modernize-*` | Modern C++ improvements: `nullptr` over `NULL`, range-based `for`, `override`, `auto` |
| `performance-*` | Performance anti-patterns: unnecessary copies, inefficient containers, missed `const` |
| `readability-*` | Code clarity: identifier naming, redundant expressions, cognitive complexity |

### Checks explicitly disabled

| Check | Reason disabled |
|---|---|
| `modernize-use-trailing-return-type` | Stylistic preference; trailing return types (`-> int`) are not universally preferred |
| `cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-array-to-pointer-decay` | Protobuf's C-style API triggers this; not actionable for our code |
| `cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-vararg` | Same: protobuf and system APIs use varargs internally |
| `cppcoreguidelines-avoid-magic-numbers` / `readability-magic-numbers` | Too noisy for protocol port numbers, group IDs, and other domain constants |
| `readability-braces-around-statements` | Conflicts with `AllowShortIfStatementsOnASingleLine` in `.clang-format` |
| `cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-pointer-arithmetic` | Protobuf internals trigger this; not actionable for our code |

### Header filter

```yaml
HeaderFilterRegex: '(adapter_iptc|adapter_socket)/include/.*'
```

clang-tidy analyses all translation units it is given, but it only reports diagnostics for headers that match this regex. This suppresses warnings from system, gtest and (later) protobuf-generated headers, keeping the output focused on project code.

---

## compile_commands.json

The CMake `configure` target passes `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON`, which tells CMake to write `production-builds/release/compile_commands.json`. This file lists every source file and the exact compiler flags used to build it.

clang-tidy reads this file via `-p production-builds/release/` to know how to parse each source file correctly — include paths, preprocessor defines, C++ standard version, etc.

The file is generated by the Release build only. The TSan and ASan builds do not export compile commands since static analysis runs on the clean Release build.

---

## `tidy` vs `tidy-fix` vs `tidy-check`

| Target | Modifies files? | Exits non-zero on issues? | Use case |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tidy` | No | No | Developer inspection — see what clang-tidy finds |
| `tidy-fix` | Yes (`--fix --fix-errors`) | No | Apply safe automatic fixes locally |
| `tidy-check` | No | Yes (`-warnings-as-errors="*"`) | CI gate — fails the build if any issue exists |

`tidy-fix` applies only fixes that clang-tidy is confident are safe and correct. Some checks produce diagnostics that require manual intervention; those are reported but not auto-fixed.

---

## How to use

```bash
# First, make sure the Release build is configured (generates compile_commands.json)
make configure   # or: make rebuild

# Inspect what clang-tidy finds
make tidy

# Auto-fix what can be fixed automatically
make tidy-fix

# CI gate (same check that runs in the pipeline)
make tidy-check
```

---

## Relationship to clang-format

| Tool | What it checks | Modifies logic? |
|---|---|---|
| `clang-format` | Style: indentation, spacing, line breaks | Never |
| `clang-tidy` | Semantics: bugs, anti-patterns, best practices | Only with `--fix` / `tidy-fix` |

Both tools are independent and complementary. `format-check` and `tidy-check` are separate CI gates that can fail independently.
